driver_cards.label: Natural Gas Price
driver_cards.interpretation: Weekly NG close used as the valuation dependent variable.

driver_cards.label: US Dollar (Broad)
driver_cards.interpretation: A firm dollar typically pressures energy commodities. Broad USD index at 120.75.

driver_cards.label: Working Gas Storage
driver_cards.interpretation: Storage is 156 Bcf above the 5-year same-week average (2827 Bcf), 5.5% surplus.

driver_cards.label: US Dry Gas Production
driver_cards.interpretation: Elevated production is typically bearish for price. Official dry natural gas production.

driver_cards.label: LNG Exports
driver_cards.concept: U.S. liquefied natural gas exports (not feedgas)
driver_cards.interpretation: Strong LNG exports are typically supportive for domestic prices (export volumes — not terminal feedgas).

driver_cards.label: Heating Degree Days
driver_cards.interpretation: Heating Degree Days anomaly -1.06σ vs sample mean (actuals only).

driver_cards.label: Cooling Degree Days
driver_cards.interpretation: Cooling Degree Days anomaly +1.77σ vs sample mean (actuals only).

driver_cards.label: Seasonality
driver_cards.interpretation: Historical Jul seasonality: avg weekly return -3.10% across 5 sample weeks in price history.

instrument.summary_text: Natural Gas currently appears approximately 29.0% undervalued. The strongest bullish driver is lng exports. The strongest bearish driver is us dollar (broad). LNG exports remain supportive. Overall institutional bias remains Bullish.
instrument.model_note: energy_natural_gas_v1: log(price) ~ storage_surplus_bcf, dry_gas_production, lng_exports, hdd_anomaly, cdd_anomaly, log_dxy, seasonality_factor (R²=0.516, n=528)
